newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier, could weaken further.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier, could weaken further.

text.p: Gold and silver prices could be about to pay the penalty for failing to take advantage of a series of positive factors, dealers and analysts said on Thursday.
Prices opened slightly weaker and the forecast was that gold values in particular could test recent lows as speculators who had anticipated higher prices lost patience with the market.
Gold was fixed at $341.80 per ounce down $2.00 from Wednesday and a close of $343.80/$344.30.

"It has had the opportunity to rally on physical demand, on the PGMs (platinum group metals) and on the possiblity of a delayed or weaker European Monetary Union and it hasn't done anything," a dealer said.
That diffidence could cost gold a trip down to its support levels this week, he added.
"Everybody has been sitting a bit long looking for a reaction. Now that the dollar is rallying, we may have to look for a test of the downside," the dealer said.
The $340.00-$338.00 support area could be tested.
Physical demand for gold at the low $340s has been high recently but dealers feared this might abate on a price fall.
"There is a good chance the physical buyers will hold off waiting for an even lower price if gold weakens," a dealer said.

The dollar firmed to over 115 yen at its peak overnight against 111.29 on Wednesday on comments from Japan's Ministry of Finance's international bureau head saying the country's trade surplus was not a concern.
The surge brought out heavy bullion selling in the Far East as investors took advantage of higher in domestic prices.
A limit-up move on the Tocom futures exchange paced by the weaker yen was pared by speculative selling into the rally.
The PGMs were subdued and palladium was lower but dealers said volatility could return if there was any sign of a glitch in Russia opening its export campaign to Japan next month.
Russia which provides over 60 percent of the world's palladium and around 25 percent of its platinumhas been out of the market since December due to adminsitrative problems.
"There is still volatility in the market. Russia has said it will export (to Japan) as soon as possible but that could still be th very end of Jule," one dealer said.
Platinum was at $445.00/$450.00 up $1,.00 and palladium was at $206.00/$211.00 down $8.20.
Silver was down two cents at $4.74/$4.76.
